audit.summary: Four demonstrated defects affect core TTM/FRM theory: incorrect depth origin in Eq. 4; invalid feature-to-coordinate inequality in Eq. 15; nonvanishing Jacobian-omission error for the unregularized dual-anchor loss; and false fusion composition law. Empirical improvements and ablations remain positive evidence for tested settings.
limitations: Limitations: No acquired author repository; historical implementation choices are unknown.
Limitations: Separate supplement availability is undetermined after the supplied HTTP 403 access failure.
Limitations: No author-code execution, model sampling, timing reproduction, or fresh empirical validation.
Limitations: All 28 pages read as text; selected critical equations and figures visually inspected, not every gallery image.
Limitations: Constructed counterexamples test printed mathematical definitions; no empirical score loss is inferred.
P1 — Counterevidence: Object-centered depth and orthographic coordinates could give a restricted repaired formula.
P1 — Counterevidence: No acquired code establishes whether a missing centering step was implemented.
P1 — Counterevidence: Reported image metrics can improve despite biased correspondence.
P2 — Counterevidence: Coordinate-only stability can follow from a Lipschitz depth estimator.
P2 — Counterevidence: Fig. 12 gives favorable empirical trajectories.
P2 — Counterevidence: Additional image and warp regularity may support a revised theorem.
P3 — Counterevidence: Figs. 10-11 show small errors and similar tested outputs.
P3 — Counterevidence: An anchor-norm lower bound, cosine regularization or detached weights changes the construction and needs explicit assumptions.
P3 — Counterevidence: Measured speedup is not refuted.
P3 — Counterevidence: A trajectory-restricted claim would require explicit loss-gradient control along the actual trajectory; the constructed full trajectory has not been established.
P4 — Counterevidence: Ordinary 3D rotation group law is valid.
P4 — Counterevidence: The heuristic adjacent-view loss may be useful without the composition theorem.
The original report's complete scope, counterevidence and unresolved questions are retained below.
This import checks publication format and identity; it does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific review is pending; author adoption has not been requested.

proposition.claim:
Location: PDF p. 5, Definition 4.1 and Eq. (4), Depth Prior Estimation

Kind: core geometric correspondence

Text: The stated camera-centered depth formula tracks corresponding points under a fixed-elevation camera orbit.

Location: PDF p. 5 Proposition 4.2/Eq. (5); p. 13 Appendix B.1/Eq. (15); Eq. (19)

Kind: core stability derivation

Text: A transformed-image difference is bounded by transformed-coordinate displacement and depth-estimation error.

Location: PDF p. 7 Theorem 4.4/Eq. (13), Eq. (14); pp. 14-15 Appendix B.3; Eqs. (7)-(11) p. 6

Kind: core acceleration theorem

Text: Omitting the noise-predictor Jacobian has gradient error tending to zero as t tends to zero.

Location: PDF p. 6 after Definition 4.3; pp. 15-16 Proposition B.2/Eqs. (29)-(30)

Kind: core operator composition

Text: (M T_alpha1)(M T_alpha2)=M T_(alpha1+alpha2) for all angles.

assumptions: Level circular look-at cameras; visible pivot marker; common principal point 100; distance 4; compatible scale; azimuth change pi/6.
Depth follows the paper's stated camera-center distance convention.
T_alpha is the declared image/feature operator on L2.
alpha=0, x0=phi, xhat0=1.1 phi, ||phi||2=1; constant, bounded-gradient depth estimator.
Current clean feature u=(sigma,0), sigma=sqrt(1-alpha)>0; adjacent blocks have seven e1 and two e2, all four corners e1.
Local derivative holds adjacent features fixed, matching the p. 6 local gradient map.
Functional input family under printed assumptions, not shown to be a complete sampling trajectory of a particular trained denoiser.
Positive collinear features Z=1+x^2+y^2 on a local image interior.
Actual dual-anchor weights become 1/9; after fusion directions remain the same.

repair.content:
Specify intrinsics/extrinsics and depth convention, or restrict to centered orthographic geometry with an offset and consistent units.

Distinguish coordinates from features; specify fixed depth, spatial regularity, distortion/visibility controls and residual bias; prove the resulting operator bound.

Use the chain-rule operator-norm bound; require uniform Jacobian and loss-gradient bounds with alpha tending to one; separately control finite-step and accumulated effects.

Remove the claim or prove a restricted result with explicit projection/idempotence and equivariance assumptions.
